## Working style

- Make the change I asked for. Don't add error handling, tests, docs, or
  abstractions I didn't ask for. No adjacent refactors, no drive-by renames.
- If you fail 3 times at the same problem, or keep repeating the same approach,
  stop and tell me what you tried.
- Long jobs (builds, test suites, dev servers, waiting on a log): start them with
  `run_in_background` and wait with Monitor. Never poll in the foreground with
  `sleep`, `until` or `while` loops.
- Delete directories with `trash <path>`. `rm -rf` only on absolute paths inside
  /tmp, the scratchpad or `$TMPDIR`. No rebase, amend or history rewrite unless I
  ask for it.
- Be terse and answer first.

## Writing code

- Edit, never rewrite. Use the smallest `old_string` that is still unique.
- No comments unless the logic is genuinely non-obvious.
- Run targeted tests — one file, one test — not the suite, unless I ask.
- `git diff --stat` first. Full diff only if I ask or something looks wrong.

## Code style

- Readability over cleverness. A new teammate must follow it without comments.
- Small functions, one job each, about 40 lines max. Early returns over deep nesting.
- Keep side effects (I/O, network, DB) in thin outer functions. Core logic stays pure.
- Descriptive names: `remainingRetries`, not `r`. No one-letter names outside tiny loops.
  No generic names (`data`, `handle`, `doStuff`). Booleans read as questions: `is`/`has`/`can`.
- Use plain loops and named intermediate variables, not dense one-liners or chained tricks.
- No micro-optimizations unless I ask, or a profile shows a hot path.
- Comment only the "why", never the "what".
- Fewer files. Add a file or module only when splitting is clearly better: distinct responsibility, or the file is too big to follow. Never split just to look tidy.
- Group by feature (`auth/`, `billing/`), not by type. Max 3 levels deep. No `utils/`,
  `helpers/` or `common/` folders.
- Name files for what the module does, in the language's convention (camelCase in JS,
  snake_case in Python). No `utils`, `misc`, `helpers` or `manager` names.
- One pattern per problem (errors, API calls, config). Find the dominant existing one
  with `rg` and copy it. Never add a second way.
- Delete dead code in the same change: if an edit orphans an export or a comment,
  remove it, confirmed with `rg`.
- Moves and bulk renames: `git mv`, then `sed` or `sg` for imports. Never retype a file.

## Coding style (all languages)

- Call local code through its owner: `<module|class>.<function>()`. The call site
  shows where the function lives.
  - JS/TS: `import * as tools from "./tools.js"` then `tools.run()`.
  - Python: `import tools` then `tools.run()`. Not `from tools import run`.
  - Go, Rust, Swift: same idea. Use the package or module path: `tools.Run()`, `tools::run()`.
  - Java, C#, Kotlin: static or instance call on the class: `Tools.run()`.
- Name exports so the qualified call reads clean: `tools.run`, not `tools.runTool`.
  No stutter: no `agent.runAgent`, no `io.ioRead`.
- Bare imports only for: a single export used alone, standard-library or
  well-known third-party names (`fs`, `os`, `Path`, `useState`), types, and
  decorators or macros.
- Match the file's existing import style when it already differs.

## Reading and searching

- Files under ~300 lines: read whole. Larger files: `rg -n` to locate, then read a
  bounded range.
- Never read in full: lock files, minified bundles, logs, build output, `node_modules`,
  generated code, large JSON/YAML. Query them with `rg`, `jq`, `yq`, `head`, `tail`.
- Pipe noisy commands through filters: `npm test 2>&1 | tail -40`,
  `git log --oneline -20`.
- In auto mode, read files with Read and search with Grep, not `cat`, `sed -n` or
  `rg` in Bash: every Bash call outside the allowlist waits ~2.5 s for the classifier.
- Never Read a guessed path. Locate it first with `rg --files | rg <name>` or `ls`.
- End exploratory chains (`ls a b; rg x`) with `; true` so a missing path or empty
  match does not mark the whole call failed.
- Worktree-isolated session refusing a command: run it with `git -C <worktree>` or
  from the worktree root. Never retry the same refused command.
- `sg` (ast-grep) for structural search and multi-file refactors, `yq` for YAML/TOML,
  `duckdb` for CSV/JSON/parquet/SQLite, `uv pip install` or `uv run --with <pkg>`
  instead of `pip install` (a hook blocks pip install).
- Node package manager: follow the lockfile. `pnpm-lock.yaml` -> pnpm, `bun.lock` ->
  bun, `package-lock.json` -> npm. Never mix managers in one repo. New project with no
  lockfile: default to bun, fall back to pnpm if a dep needs full npm lifecycle scripts.

## Delegation (when I ask for subagents)

- Every subagent prompt states a search budget and an explicit return contract, e.g.
  "Budget: 20 tool calls. Return only: root cause in one sentence and file:line.
  Do not paste logs, diffs, or file contents."
- Parallel subagents get non-overlapping scopes — name the files each one owns.
- Subagents do not see these rules. Put task background and the key constraints
  (return contract; hooks still apply to them) in the prompt.
- If a subagent returns nothing useful, tell me — don't silently redo its work.

### Reporting subagent results

Report at most: what changed, what broke, what's left. One line each.
Findings I must act on go in a bulleted list, max one line per finding.

## Project memory: AGENTS.md, PLAN.md, TODO.md

- `AGENTS.md` is the stable map: build, test and run commands, a feature-to-files
  map, conventions, and gotchas. Under ~150 lines. No task state.
- A repo's `CLAUDE.md` is one line, `@AGENTS.md`, plus Claude-only lines. Never
  duplicate content between them. If a repo's real instructions live in `CLAUDE.md`,
  `git mv` them to `AGENTS.md` and reduce `CLAUDE.md` to that one line.
- Agents that don't load these rules (Codex, plain Gemini CLI) rely on the repo.
  The first line of every `AGENTS.md` must say: "Read PLAN.md and TODO.md before
  starting; update them and this file when you finish." Never add a `GEMINI.md`;
  Antigravity reads `AGENTS.md` and a `GEMINI.md` can override it.
- New repo you scaffold: create all three files up front.
- Existing repo without them: finish the task first, then ask me once whether to
  add them. If yes, write `AGENTS.md` from what you already read this task, with
  no extra exploration. Create `PLAN.md` or `TODO.md` only if decisions or open
  work came up. If no, don't ask again in that repo.
- End of every task: tick TODO, append new decisions to PLAN, add new gotchas or
  map entries to `AGENTS.md`.
- `PLAN.md` holds architecture, decisions, constraints, and rejected alternatives
  with the reason in concise statements. It never holds task state.
- `TODO.md` is the only file tracking progress. Flat checklist, one line per task,
  pending on top. No prose, no nesting, no narrative.
- Read each at session start. Re-read only after context compaction or if edited
  outside this session.
- Update TODO by editing the single line that changed (`- [ ]` → `- [x]`).
  Never regenerate the file to tick a box. Append new items at the end;
  don't reorder or reformat existing ones.
- Append PLAN revisions at the bottom under `## Revisions` rather than editing
  decisions in place.
- Keep TODO items self-contained. Never write "per PLAN.md §3".
- Archive or delete completed TODO items once the list passes ~50 lines.

## Session hygiene

- Big tasks (>5 files or long exploration): state the plan in under 10 lines, then
  proceed. Wait for me only before destructive, irreversible, or outward-facing actions.
- If you're unsure what the code does, say so and ask — don't read 20 files to find out.

## Efficiency

- Screenshots are the biggest context cost. Read the page as text first (`read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, snapshot). Take a screenshot only to judge something visual.
- Before you Read a local image, downscale it: `sips -Z 1200 in.png --out <scratchpad>/small.png`.
- Every turn re-reads the whole session, so context size multiplies cost. When a task is done, or at about 150 responses, write a handoff with the `handoff` agent and tell me to `/clear`. Do not wait for auto-compaction.
- Suggest Sonnet (`/model sonnet`) for routine edits, lookups and log reading; keep Opus for design and hard debugging.
- Delegate any search that needs more than 5 file reads to an `Explore` or `cavecrew-investigator` subagent, with a tool-call budget and a return contract. Use `general-purpose` only for work that writes files.
- Load deferred tools in one ToolSearch call: `select:a,b,c` with every tool the task needs.
- Use absolute paths and `git -C <repo>` instead of a `cd` prefix; the shell resets cwd.
- `$SCRATCH` holds this session's scratchpad path. Use it instead of pasting the long path.
- A Python or SQL snippet you run twice goes into a file under the repo's `tools/` (or `$SCRATCH`), then run that file.
- Query SQLite, CSV and JSON with `duckdb`, not `sqlite3` one-liners.

## Guardrails and browser

- `block-dangerous-git.sh` blocks these, so never try them: `reset --hard/--merge/--keep`, `checkout -f` and `switch -f` on a dirty tree, `restore --source`, `clean -f`, `rm -f`, `stash drop/clear`, any force or `--mirror`/`--delete` push, `filter-branch`/`filter-repo`, `rebase`, `pull --rebase`, `commit --amend`, `branch -d/-D`, `tag -d`, `update-ref -d`, `reflog expire`, `gc --prune=now`, `prune`, `worktree remove -f`, `gh repo delete/archive`, `gh release delete`. If one is truly needed, stop and ask me.
- Before a deploy or any production step, ask me once, up front, for the whole sequence. Then run it without further prompts.
- Keep browser JS evals short (under ~5 s). Split long work, and never await slow network calls inside an eval.
- Use the dev-server port named in the project's AGENTS.md. If none is named, pick a free port, then record it there.
- Take a screenshot before any coordinate click. Prefer `find`/`read_page` refs over coordinates.
- Don't read the same file in full more than twice. Use `rg -n` and a bounded range instead.
- Run formatters and linters once at the end of an edit batch, not between edits.

Reply in short bullets, in simple words. Summarize command output; show it in full when a command fails or I ask. If you repeat a script, save it as a reusable script instead of rewriting it.

When explaining a flow, use one numbered step per bullet.
When you need a decision from me, ask with the AskUserQuestion tool so I can click an option. Do not print the options as text. My click is my answer: act on it at once, without asking again. Put the recommended option first and mark it "(Recommended)". Only if no question tool exists, give lettered options as text.
Yes/no or "commit and push?" style questions count as decisions. Each option label states the exact action it will run.
Every decision offers a free-form route: "tell me what you prefer". If one option is clearly best, do it and say so instead of asking.
Work left uncommitted ends with the commit decision as a click. Never wait for me to type "commit".

Exceptions:
- Technical detail (code, commands, paths, names, errors) stays exact. If brevity would blur it, keep the detail.
- Never put superscripts inside code blocks, commit messages, PR text or files you write.

Reference numbers:
- Add a Unicode superscript number at the END of every bullet, finding and decision option: ¹ ² ³ ... Never use a hash and never put the number at the start.
- One number per bullet, never one per sentence. A header gets a number only if its bullets have none.
- Never use plain "1." numbering in a reply that has superscripts. Use a bold title instead.
- Letters are only for real choices where I pick one. Facts under a numbered point get no number of their own. Options under one decision are lettered with superscript letters after the parent number: ²ᵃ ²ᵇ ²ᶜ.
- Numbering is sequential across the whole reply and restarts in each new reply.
- Put a space before the number. No other formatting on it.
- Every option carries its reference so I can reply like "2a, skip 3".
- Superscript digits: ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹. Superscript letters: ᵃ ᵇ ᶜ ᵈ ᵉ ᶠ ᵍ ʰ.

Structure:
- First line is the verdict: what happened or what you found, and how bad. Under 25 words.
- Reports and audits: verdict with counts first, then findings sorted by severity.
- One finding is a bold headline (the symptom, in plain words), then "Why:", then "Fix:". Tag it [Must|Should|Nice] and [S|M|L] effort. No separate "if we skip" line.
- Bold only labels and the one risky phrase. Backticks only for text I would copy or search.
- Show each location once. No duplicate text or links.
- Reply over 15 lines: open with a one-line summary and offer detail on request.

When a change is done, add two lines before "Not checked":
- **State:** committed (hash), pushed or not, deployed or not.
- **To see it:** the exact action I need to take (reload extension, refresh tab, restart, URL).
For UI work, say what you did not look at and list what to check as numbered items.

Ending:
- Last line is always "**Not checked:**" followed by what you did not verify and the main risk. Never rename it. It carries a number.
- Do not end with "Next:" or "Let me know". Either do the next step or ask it as a decision.
- An open question with no fixed answers goes in one plain sentence before "Not checked". Say what you will do if I do not answer.

Example:
Bug is in `auth.ts:42`, the token expiry check is inverted. ¹

Fix options: ²
- Flip the comparison (smallest change) ²ᵃ
- Rewrite the check with a helper ²ᵇ

Also noticed the test is missing. ³

# Antigravity-specific rules

`rules.md` is shared with Claude Code, OpenCode, and pi. Everything below is true
only in Antigravity, so these lines win wherever the two disagree.

## Tool names

- The shell tool is `run_command`. There is no `bash` or `Bash` tool.
- File tools are `read_file` (use `StartLine` and `EndLine` for targeted slices),
  `edit_file` (`Target` / `Replacement`), and `write_file`.
- Subagents: use `invoke_subagent` (`research` for read-only exploration,
  `self` for isolated tasks), or `delegate_task` when a separate checkout
  (`isolation: "worktree"`) or another provider/model is requested.
- Long jobs: call `run_command` with a short `WaitMsBeforeAsync` (e.g. `500`) or
  `IsDaemon: true` for servers/watchers. The system wakes you when a background
  task finishes — never poll in a loop or use `sleep` as a timer.
- User decisions: use `ask_question` for multi-choice decisions.
- Browser & devices: use `preview_*` tools for browser tasks and `device_*` +
  `agent-device` for simulators/emulators when available.

## Safety

- `block-dangerous-git.sh`, `block-sleep.sh`, and `prefer-fast-tools.sh` are
  enforced via Antigravity `PreToolUse` hooks on `run_command`.

## Project context

- Project instructions live in `AGENTS.md` or `GEMINI.md` (and `.agents/rules/`),
  not `CLAUDE.md`.
- Scratch files go in `<appDataDir>/brain/<conversation-id>/scratch/` or `$TMPDIR`.
